In order to remedy this inconveniency, government has found no better expedient than to impose
upon the whole generality an additional tax of 120,000 livers.
This additional tax is rated upon all the different districts subject to the tale according
to the old assessment, but it is levied only upon those which, in the actual state of things,
are by that assessment under tax, and it is applied to the relief of those which, by the
Two districts, for example, one of which ought, in the actual state of things, to be taxed
at 900, the other at 1,100 livers, are, by the old assessment, both taxed at 1,000 livers.
Both these districts are, by the additional tax, rated at 1,100 livers each.
But this additional tax is levied only upon the district undercharged, and it is applied
altogether to the relief of that overcharged, which consequently pays only 900 livers.
The government neither gains nor loses by the additional tax, which is applied altogether
to remedy the inequalities arising from the old assessment.
The application is pretty much regulated according to the discretion of the intendant of the
generality, and must, therefore, be in a great measure arbitrary.
